title: Distance Set Diameter: Linear vs Logarithmic Growth Gap
description: Analyzes the gap between the known diameter bound Ω(n/log n) from Guth–Katz and the conjectured linear bound Ω(n) for integer distance sets. Proves the gap factor log n grows without bound, n/log n = o(n), and the linear conjecture implies the known bound. States the Anning–Erdős finiteness constraint.

meta.author: Guth–Katz (2015), Erdős (1986); analysis formalized 2026
meta.assumptions: One sorry: Anning–Erdős finiteness theorem (requires number theory + geometry argument).

overview.historicalContext: Erdős Problem #100 asks whether n-point integer distance sets must have diameter ≫ n. The Guth–Katz 2015 distinct distances theorem gives diam ≥ cn/log n. The conjecture is diam ≥ cn (linear). The gap is exactly log n.
overview.problemStatement: **Question**: Is the diameter of n-point integer distance sets Θ(n) or Θ(n/log n)?
overview.text: Formalizes the growth rate gap between known and conjectured bounds for integer distance set diameters.
